home_pitcher_note: Halladay returns as the ace of a relatively young and inexperienced starting staff, taking the ball on Opening Day for the seventh year in a row. That streak is the longest such run for any pitcher in Toronto franchise history. Halladay finished last season as the runner-up to Cleveland's Cliff Lee in the balloting for the American League Cy Young Award in 2008, ending the campaign with a career-high 206 strikeouts and a league-leading nine complete games. Halladay compiled 246 innings -- the third season in a row Doc logged at least 220 innings -- and he led the AL with a 2.08 ground ball-to-fly ball ratio and a strikeout-to-walk rate of 5.28. During that impressive showing, Halladay did not encounter the Tigers, but he has handled Detroit well over his career. In 15 outings against his Opening Day opponent, Halladay has gone 11-2 with a crisp 1.93 ERA. Pitching at Rogers Centre has also been something that Halladay has enjoyed over his career. Using his dancing and darting arsenal of sinkers and cutters, Halladay has fashioned a 73-28 mark at the Dome with a 3.28 ERA over 135 games. Last year, all Halladay did in Toronto was go 10-4 with a 2.78 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The former All-Star's effort to bounce back from last year's shocking struggles begins here, with his second straight Opening Day assignment. His 1-7 record over the first month and a half last season sent him reeling toward an American League high in losses and a spiral he couldn't seem to escape no matter what adjustments he tried to make. He believes he has made the changes he needed, and he has the Spring Training performances to back it up -- one run allowed over a 19-inning stretch, including a 13-inning scoreless streak over his final three Spring Training starts before the Braves roughed him up in his finale for seven runs on nine hits over five innings. A return to a lower arm angle seems to have helped bring back much of his old velocity, bumping the fastball to 97 mph, while a change of stance with his landing leg is expected to help give him better command on all of his pitches. Part of last year's struggles included an Aug. 11 loss to the Blue Jays at Comerica Park in his first career outing against Toronto, which hit him for six runs on seven hits in 4 1/3 innings, the fourth straight loss in a season that included three different four-game losing streaks, two of them in the season's second half.

home_pitcher_note: Purcey is third on Toronto's depth chart, but has been moved up into the second slot in the rotation to break up the right-handed and left-handed starters. Purcey had an inconsistent stint as a rookie starter for the Jays last season, finishing with 58 strikeouts and 29 walks over 65 innings in 12 starts. Purcey -- a first-round pick by Toronto in the 2004 First-Year Player Draft -- pitches best when he has his curveball working well and he's consistently finding the strike zone. The left-hander can be exposed when his breaking ball isn't working properly.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson's Tigers debut will come against one of his familiar division foes from his days in Tampa Bay, not to mention an opponent he faced little more than a week ago. There are likely no secrets between Jackson and the Jays, but both he and the Tigers believe that if he executes his stuff, it likely won't matter. He went 2-1 over his four starts against Toronto last year, allowing nine earned runs over 24 1/3 innings. At Rogers Centre, however, he has never lost in five career starts, striking out 28 batters over 33 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: At 24 years old, and with just two big league seasons under his belt, Litsch is the most experienced starter on the staff behind ace Roy Halladay. The right-hander has gone 20-18 with a 3.67 ERA over the past two years. Litsch works fast, fields his position well and pounds the strike zone. Last season, he added a four-seam fastball to his repertoire, helping to offset his cutter and sinker. After finishing with 196 innings between Toronto and Triple-A a year ago, Litsch is hoping to top 200 innings for the Blue Jays this season.
away_pitcher_note: Jeremy Bonderman's season-opening DL stint with shoulder tightness means that Miner, who has had two successful summer stints as a starter over the past three years, gets to open the season in a rotation for the first time in his brief Major League career. And he'll do it after manager Jim Leyland had just about ruled him out of contention for a starting job. He struggled with hanging sinkers and big hits while he was actually a starting candidate, then turned in 10 straight scoreless innings once he was ruled out. He has been incredibly effective against the Jays in his career, tossing 16 2/3 innings with three earned runs allowed.

home_pitcher_note: Romero, who was the first pitcher selected (sixth overall) in the 2005 First-Year Player Draft, beat out fellow left-handed prospects Brett Cecil and Brad Mills for a spot in the rotation this spring. Romero, 24, was considered out of the race after a handful of spring outings, but pitching coach Brad Arnsberg went to work on retooling the lefty's delivery and results came fast. Romero impressed the Jays in his last two Spring Training starts and convinced the club to take him north. Last season, Romero was 8-8 with a 4.55 ERA in 28 Minor League starts between Double-A and Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: Less than two years after Porcello graduated from high school, he formally graduates to the big leagues. The Tigers' first-round Draft pick from 2007 accelerated his timetable dramatically and earned a rotation job with a consistent, solid spring and a bunch of nasty sinkers for quick ground ball outs, not to mention a maturity well beyond his tender age of 20. He was on a 75-pitch limit last year at Class A ball, but the Tigers appear inclined to let him go longer as the season goes along.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis beat out five other candidates for this spot in the rotation by displaying the type of fastball command that won him four games in as many starts at the big-league level last September. But after being named to the rotation, Lewis' spring stats quickly derailed, as he gave up 15 runs on 21 hits in his last 6 2/3 innings of Cactus League play. Lewis is a finesse lefty who needs to have precise command to be effective, because he doesn't have dominant stuff. When he's on, he can be brilliant, as evidenced by the eight scoreless innings he tossed against the Orioles in his Major League debut. He has never faced the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Richmond -- a rookie at 29 years old -- opens the season in Toronto's rotation after making just five starts for the club in his first professional season in 2008. Richmond is a native of North Vancouver, British Columbia, and was signed as a non-drafted free agent two winters ago following three years in the Independent League with the Edmonton Cracker Cats. Richmond opened his first pro tour at Double-A and was quickly moved to Triple-A and then to the big leagues. Richmond had an inconsistent spring after missing time for the World Baseball Classic, but the Jays decided to hand him the fifth spot over prospect Brad Mills.

home_pitcher_note: Lee will be kept on four days' rest for this start, with fifth starter Anthony Reyes held back a day. He's coming off a rough Opening Day loss against the Rangers, as he gave up seven runs on 10 hits with a walk and five strikeouts in five innings. This followed a spring in which he posted a 12.46 ERA, so there are certainly concerns about his effectiveness at this early juncture. Lee didn't give up his seventh run of the '08 season until his eight start of the season -- on May 18. He is 1-3 with 4.02 ERA in seven career starts against the Blue Jays. Last season, he went 1-0 against them, giving up no earned runs in 17 innings over two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay took the mound at Rogers Centre on Monday for his seventh consecutive Opening Day start, extending his own club record for season-opening outings. Doc was sharp through six innings, allowing just two hits among the first 20 batters he faced. Working with an ample cushion of run support, though, Halladay slipped some in the seventh inning, surrendering four runs -- two on a homer to Detroit's Brandon Inge. Even so, Halladay picked up his third Opening Day win, tying a franchise record. He finished with two strikeouts, one walk and 11 outs on ground balls. Halladay is 5-2 with a 3.73 ERA in 12 career games against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired in a midseason trade with the Cardinals last year, Reyes wowed the Indians with his performance in August, when his 2.01 ERA was the third-best in the AL. But Reyes comes with a catch, in the form of a chronic elbow condition that will have to be monitored all season. The Indians are aiming to protect him by placing him in their fifth rotation spot. Reyes tweaked his mechanics over the offseason, and he had a healthy and effective spring camp. He is best remembered for pitching the Cardinals to a victory in Game 1 of the 2006 World Series, but he hopes to keep his elbow in check and make a new name for himself with the Tribe.
away_pitcher_note: In his season debut on Tuesday, Purcey gave the Blue Jays exactly what they need from him this season. The left-hander lasted seven innings, yielding three runs -- two earned -- on five hits with five strikeouts and three walks. Purcey, who finished with 101 pitches -- 61 strikes -- didn't use his changeup once, opting to stick with an array of fastballs, sliders and curves. When he did slip out of the strike zone, Purcey was able to correct himself quickly and limit the damage. Purcey faced the Indians once last season, allowing three runs on six hits over six innings in a losing effort.

home_pitcher_note: Usually known for his stellar command of his pitches, Slowey struggled to make adjustments early in his last start against the Mariners. But when the Twins really needed him to settle down, Slowey did just that, managing to toss six innings and allow five runs on nine hits. He had one wild pitch in the contest that scored a run, which is an unusual occurrence for the pitcher who had just one wild pitch in 27 starts last year. Now Slowey will have to see if he can relax and keep his pitches down when he faces the Blue Jays. He is 0-2 with a 5.51 ERA in three career starts vs. Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: Litsch struggled in his season debut on Wednesday, matching an unfortunate career high with three home runs allowed. The 24-year-old right-hander gave up two blasts to Tigers slugger Miguel Cabrera -- both on sinkers -- and yielded another on a cutter to Brandon Inge. Overall, Litsch was tagged for five runs on seven hits and finished with five strikeouts and one walk over six innings, finishing with 106 pitches (64 strikes). In his career against the Twins, Litsch is 3-0 with a 2.08 ERA in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins delivered a stellar outing in his first start of the season, allowing just one run on five hits over eight innings to the Mariners. But it was not enough to get him the win as Seattle's left-hander Jarrod Washburn held the Twins scoreless over eight innings. Perkins' eight-inning outing tied his career high and while he threw 106 pitches in the start, he could have gone longer had it not been for two, 11-pitch at-bats by the Mariners in the seventh inning. Next up for Perkins will be a start against the Blue Jays. In two career starts against Toronto, Perkins is 0-0 with a 4.91 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Romero was part of a unique moment in baseball history on Thursday afternoon. Romero (the sixth overall pick in the 2005 First-Year Player Draft) squared off against Detroit starter Rick Porcello (27th overall in the '07 Draft). It marked the first time since the Draft began in 1965 that a pair of first-round picks faced each other in their respective Major League debuts. Romero came out on top, limiting the Tigers to two runs on seven hits with five strikeouts and two walks over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Baker will make his first start of the season against the Blue Jays. The right-hander began the year on the disabled list with right shoulder stiffness. It was not a problem that the Twins felt would keep Baker out for long, but they didn't want to risk it considering that Baker had trouble keeping his arm loose between innings during his final Spring Training outing. All of that appears to be behind Baker now and he'll focus on building off his success last season. The right-hander has shown more consistency in each of the last two seasons and showed his focus under pressure by going 3-0 with 2.53 ERA during the Twins' pennant chase last September. Baker is 0-1 with a 3.72 ERA in three starts vs. Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: In his season debut on Friday, Richmond was only able to work four innings against the Indians before a lengthy rain delay -- the longest in Jays franchise history -- forced him from the game. In his abbreviated appearance, the 29-year-old rookie allowed three runs on five hits with four strikeouts and two walks in a no-decision. The three runs Richmond allowed were each driven in by Cleveland's Travis Hafner, who tagged the pitcher for a two-run double and a solo homer. Richmond has never faced the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano had problems with his command in his last start against the White Sox. The left-hander allowed five runs on six hits over his 4 2/3 innings on Saturday, but it was his four walks that stood out in the contest. Two of those scored runs as Liriano issued free passes to Jermaine Dye and Paul Konerko with the bases loaded. Next up he'll face the Blue Jays at home. This will be Liriano's first career start vs. Toronto. He pitched two scoreless innings of relief in his only appearance against the club.
away_pitcher_note: After a shaky season debut, Halladay rebounded with a strong showing against the Indians on Saturday. Over seven innings, Doc yielded only one run -- courtesy of an RBI double off the bat of Grady Sizemore -- on five hits. The ace of Toronto's staff finished with seven strikeouts, two walks and 12 outs created via grounders. In his career against the Twins, Halladay is 7-0 with a 2.92 ERA in 11 outings. Halladay has gone 3-0 with a 4.46 ERA in his career at the Metrodome.

away_pitcher_note: Outman gave up three runs, all earned, and six hits over 4 1/3 innings in his season debut Saturday against Seattle, getting no decision. Outman, 24, has never faced the Blue Jays. That's not surprising. He's faced just five teams (Mariners, Angels, Tigers, Royals and Rangers) in his brief Major League career. Outman came to the A's last July as part of the trade that sent starter Joe Blanton to Philadelphia. He went 1-2 with a 4.56 ERA with the A's in 2008, starting four games and making six appearances. He had 19 strikeouts with only eight walks. That strikeout-to-walk ratio mirrors his Minor League numbers. Throughout a Minor League career spanning 107 appearances from 2005-2008, Outman struck out 429 batters and walked 211.

home_pitcher_note: Right-hander Jesse Litsch exited his start on Monday with soreness in his pitching elbow and forearm and was placed on the 15-day disabled list. Litsch threw just 51 pitches and was charged with four runs on seven hits with three strikeouts in three-plus innings. Toronto recalled left-hander Bill Murphy to add another arm to its taxed bullpen, and moved Tallet into the rotation. Tallet will have a pitch count of around 70 for his first start since the 2006 season.
away_pitcher_note: One of two 21-year-olds in Oakland's starting rotation, Cahill was as good as he's been as a professional in his second big league start, taking a no-hitter into the seventh inning Sunday against the Mariners. Adrian Beltre's one-out single in the seventh ended Cahill's bid for history, former Oakland designated hitter Mike Sweeney's two-out double ended the shutout, and Cahill got stuck with a 1-0 loss. Armed with an outstanding sinker, Cahill walked three, hit a batter and struck out three over seven innings against Seattle; only three of the 18 outs he recorded before the seventh were hit in the air.

home_pitcher_note: Romero wasn't afforded the luxury of run support in his last outing and he walked away with a no-decision after a strong outing on the road against the Twins. In eight innings on Tuesday, Romero gave up two runs on eight hits and finished with two strikeouts and no walks. The left-hander retired the first nine hitters of the game in order and escaped a bases-loaded, no-outs jam in the sixth inning. Over 14 innings in his first two Major League starts, Romero has given up four runs on 15 hits with seven strikeouts and two walks.
away_pitcher_note: Unsatisfied with his quality start (six innings, three runs) on Opening Night, Braden was quite a bit better in his second assignment of the season, working into the seventh inning and holding the Red Sox to two runs on six hits and a walk while striking out three. Braden, 25, has made one appearance against the Jays since breaking into the big leagues in 2007, allowing three earned runs over 2 2/3 innings. Not a particularly hard thrower, Braden excels when he's commanding the ball to both sides of the plate and isn't afraid to throw his "plus" changeup or tight slider when behind in the count.

home_pitcher_note: The ace of the staff has won all three of his starts this year. In his last outing against the Twins, he allowed one run on eight hits and struck out eight in seven innings. Opponents are batting .238 against him with an on-base percentage of .274. Last year against Texas, he was 1-1 with a 2.50 ERA but in his career is 7-6 with a 5.34 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy allowed three runs in six innings in a quality start against the Orioles on Tuesday, but the Rangers ended up losing, 7-5, in extra innings. He's allowed nine hits in 11 innings over two starts and struck out 12 but has walked seven batters. He has also allowed four home runs. He is 1-2 with a 4.05 ERA in six career appearances against the Blue Jays.

home_pitcher_note: Purcey continues to struggle with his command. In his no-decision against the Athletics in his last start, he allowed four walks and five runs in 3 2/3 innings. He has allowed 13 walks in 15 1/3 innings but his 17 strikeouts show that he has good stuff. The problem seems to be focus and concentration. He can be good one inning and not so good the next.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison took the loss in Friday's 12-3 loss to the Royals, allowing six runs in five-plus innings on eight hits and four walks. In two starts, left-handed hitters are batting .231 (3-for-13) against Harrison, while right-handers are hitting .438 with 14 hits in 32 at-bats. Overall, opponents are 3-for-18 (.167) against Harrison with runners in scoring position. Harrison is 4-2 with a 4.95 ERA in six career road starts. This will be Harrison's first career start against the Blue Jays.

home_pitcher_note: It will be Richmond's first start in more than a week. He earned his first victory of the season in his last start by allowing the Twins four hits and two runs (one earned) in 6 1/3 innings. He walked three and struck out three. He has an opponents batting average of .225 in his two starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood threw a complete game for the Rangers on Saturday but still lost, 2-0, to Zack Greinke and the Royals. In 23 innings this season, he has allowed 14 hits and four walks while striking out 14. Left-handed hitters are batting .150 off him while right-handers are hitting .205. Millwood is 1-3 with a 6.45 ERA in seven career starts against the Blue Jays. That's his second highest ERA against any AL team. But he is 1-1 with a 4.85 ERA against them in five starts over the past four seasons.

home_pitcher_note: The wild streak that knocked down Floyd last Monday at Comerica Park, when he issued seven free passes in five innings and threw just 49 of his 98 pitches for strikes, certainly was not present during Sunday's victory over the Rays. Floyd allowed two runs on six hits over seven innings, striking out seven and not issuing a single free pass. His only true mistake came in the seventh, when Ben Zobrist touched him up for a two-run home run. Floyd has a 0-1 career record against the Blue Jays with a 4.32 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Tallet made his first start since 2006 against Oakland on Saturday, replacing the injured Jesse Litsch (right forearm/elbow). He gave up two runs (one earned) on four hits in 5 1/3 innings on his way to a no-decision. Tallet threw 67 pitches in his last outing while on a strict pitch count of 70-75, and the plan is to increase that total to 85-90 pitches in his next start.
summary: 2009-04-24 - Toronto Blue Jays (14) @ Chicago White Sox (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Even without his best stuff on Saturday night against the Rays, Buehrle did what he does best -- he worked deep into the contest and gave the White Sox a chance to win. Buehrle allowed three runs on eight hits over 6 2/3 innings, striking out five and walking three. He had a stretch of 17 straight batters retired -- dating back to his last start -- end in the first inning on an Evan Longoria single. Buehrle has a 4-3 career mark and 2.66 ERA against the Blue Jays, and he finished with a 1-1 mark and a 0.59 ERA when facing Toronto in 2008.
away_pitcher_note:
After placing Ricky Romero (right oblique strain) on the 
15-day disabled list, Burres gets this start. Burres is 0-2 in two starts and one relief appearance in Triple-A this year, with an ERA of 6.97 in 10 1/3 innings. Burres gave up 11 hits and two walks while striking out seven over that span.
summary: 2009-04-25 - Toronto Blue Jays (2) @ Chicago White Sox (10) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Contreras is still searching for his first win of 2009 -- and hoping he can find the strike zone with a little more regularity. He took the loss in a 10-3 defeat at Baltimore on Tuesday, throwing only 58 of his 100 pitches for strikes. Contreras insists he's recovered from the ruptured left Achilles that short-circuited his 2008 season, but he's not instilling a lot of confidence in his team by being unable to make it through six innings in any of his previous three starts. Walks hadn't been a problem until the loss to the Orioles, when Contreras issued six free passes.
away_pitcher_note: After winning his first three starts of the season, Halladay took the loss against Texas on Tuesday, giving up five earned runs on eight hits. Halladay surrendered two home runs but punched out nine batters in an eight-inning appearance -- his longest outing of the season. He's allowed only three walks in four starts and 29 innings so far this year.
summary: 2009-04-26 - Toronto Blue Jays (4) @ Chicago White Sox (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Bannister made a dramatic comeback from Triple-A Omaha, arriving at Cleveland to pitch six shutout innings in a 2-0 victory last Wednesday night over the Indians. He looked like his old self, meaning the Bannister of 2007 when he had a highly successful rookie season for the Royals. He had just one strikeout but kept the Indians off balance and gave up just four singles on a cold night. Bannister sounded as if he expected to be going up-and-down between Kansas City and Omaha this summer, depending on the rotation needs. But with more outings like this he'll become a permanent fixture once again.
away_pitcher_note:
Purcey was in line for his first win of the season
Wednesday but closer B.J. Ryan blew the save in a game the Blue Jays eventually won, 8-7, in extra
innings. Purcey went 5 1/3 innings against Texas, giving up three runs, all earned, on seven hits. He had
struggled with his command in his previous two starts, walking a total of 10 batters in 8 1/3 innings, but
issued only two walks in Wednesday's no-decision.
summary: 2009-04-27 - Toronto Blue Jays (1) @ Kansas City Royals (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Meche pitched seven terrific innings last Thursday at Cleveland, retiring 16 straight batters at one point, before running into some trouble in the eighth inning. He left with the game tied 2-2, and reliever Ron Mahay gave up a three-run homer that dealt Meche the loss. Meche struck out seven and walked none, running up 113 pitches after getting an extra day of rest between starts. Although he'd experienced some stiffness in his previous start at Texas, because of what he termed a flat mound, he had no physical problems at Cleveland. Meche was 0-2 versus Toronto last year despite giving up just five runs in two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Richmond worked six solid innings against the Texas Rangers on Thursday, allowing only two runs and two walks on six hits. He struck out a career-high eight batters. Richmond also won his previous start -- a 12-2 victory in Minnesota -- giving him wins in back-to-back starts for the first time in his career. He has never faced Kansas City.
summary: 2009-04-28 - Toronto Blue Jays (8) @ Kansas City Royals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Greinke had his string of scoreless innings snapped at 38 last Friday night against the Tigers, but it was an unearned run and that was virtually the only flaw in his performance. It was his second straight game in which he went the distance and also struck out 10, giving him 36 Ks in just 29 innings. He threw just 108 pitches, disposing of the Tigers in a swift 2:06. Greinke stuck primarily with his fastball for the first five innings but, over the last four, had all of his pitches working. He issued just one walk, after having none in his previous 2-0 win at Texas.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday night, Tallet handcuffed the White Sox for 5 2/3 innings, blanking Chicago over that span en route to his first win as a starter since 2002. The left-hander finished with five strikeouts, three walks and four hits allowed in the victory. Tallet, who moved out of the bullpen and into the rotation to fill in for injured starter Jesse Litsch, has yielded only one run over 11 innings across two starts. In his career against the Royals, Tallet is 1-0 with a 5.79 ERA in six games.
summary: 2009-04-29 - Toronto Blue Jays (3) @ Kansas City Royals (11) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Davies had his roughest outing this season last Saturday night as the Tigers rocked him for seven runs on eight hits, two of them homers, in his 5 1/3 innings. He had surrendered just one homer in his previous 18 2/3 innings. Davies didn't have the high-quality changeup he showed in his first three starts, and his slider was staying in the middle of the plate. As he'd done in his previous outing at Texas, when he walked five including four in the first inning, he was pitching behind in the count. This time, though, he walked only two, so that was a plus.
away_pitcher_note: Burres will make his second start of the season as a fill-in for injured left-hander Ricky Romero (right oblique strain), who is expected to be sidelined until around the middle of May. In his season debut with the Jays on Saturday, Burres allowed six runs on seven hits with two strikeouts and four walks in just 4 1/3 innings in a loss to the White Sox. In his career against the Royals, Burres is 0-1 with a 3.75 ERA.
summary: 2009-04-30 - Toronto Blue Jays (6) @ Kansas City Royals (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Halladay struggled to keep a few of his pitches in the lower half of the strike zone in his most recent start, but he recovered and pitched well enough to earn a road victory over the White Sox. In seven innings in Chicago, Halladay allowed three runs on eight hits, ending with six strikeouts, one walk and 119 pitches. Halladay will face the Orioles in Toronto's first game of the season against an American League East opponent. He is 18-4 with a 2.86 ERA in 28 career games against Baltimore.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander had troubles with home runs and leadoff hitters in last Saturday's 6-5 loss to the Rangers. Hendrickson gave up homers to the leadoff hitters in each of the first three innings to help put the Orioles in an early five-run hole. He's had problems early in his last two starts, losses to the Red Sox and Rangers. Hendrickson's been good at times but hasn't found the consistency the Orioles need from a starter.

home_pitcher_note: Ray has made two Minor League starts this season, going 0-1 with a 2.25 ERA in one outing each with Class A Dunedin and Triple-A Las Vegas. On Sunday, the 25-year-old right-hander logged 4 1/3 innings and allowed no runs on two hits with three strikeouts and three walks in a no-decision for Vegas. Ray was a seventh-round pick by Toronto in the 2005 First-Year Player Draft.
away_pitcher_note: Bergesen started well but struggled at the end of his second Major League start last Sunday against Texas. The right-hander gave up two runs on five hits through four innings before the first five Rangers got hits in the fifth and ended his day. Bergesen again showed good control and command, but Orioles manager Dave Trembley said his ball wasn't sinking and moving as much. Bergesen is more of a finesse pitcher, not a power guy, and can put the ball anywhere he wants it.

home_pitcher_note: Richmond is coming off a career-high seven-inning outing against the Royals on Tuesday. He allowed just five hits and one run over that span and continues to be a positive force for a Toronto pitching staff which has been hit with a siege of injuries. Richmond was workmanlike in Kansas City and continues to trust his stuff. He got through seven on 106 pitches and helped himself with an aggressive fielding play  in the third which enabled the Jays to wiggle out of a jam.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie has surrendered a seven-run and a four-run lead in his last three outings, and he hasn't completed seven innings yet this season. By this point last year he had completed seven innings twice. Guthrie has also allowed four earned runs twice this season. Last year, he did it eight times in 30 starts. Still, Guthrie is enthusiastic about the way he's pitched and eager for his next start.

home_pitcher_note: Tallet is coming off a rough outing in an 11-3 loss at Kansas City. He had trouble finishing off the Royals with two outs and was charged with 10 earned runs over four innings. Tallet talked about leaving too many pitches over the plate and up in key situations, but chalked it up as just one bad performance after blanking the White Sox through 5 2/3 innings on four hits in his previous start.
away_pitcher_note: Facing the Red Sox on Wednesday, Carmona went 6 2/3 innings in which he more closely resembled his 19-win form of 2007. Though he walked four batters, Carmona never lost his composure. He allowed just two runs on five hits with three strikeouts. He was saddled with a no-decision after the bullpen squandered the 5-2 lead he left behind. Walks are still very much an issue for Carmona. He's issued 16 walks in 28 2/3 innings. But in this latest start, he showed better command of his secondary pitches. He is 2-0 with a 1.88 ERA in two career starts against the Blue Jays.

home_pitcher_note: Considered the Blue Jays' top pitching prospect, Cecil will make his big-league debut after a rough opening month with Triple-A Las Vegas. In four starts in the Minors, Cecil went 0-3 with an 8.31 ERA, amassing nine strikeouts and eight walks over 17 1/3 innings. On Tuesday, the lefty gave up three runs on four hits with five strikeouts and one walk in six innings for Vegas. Cecil, who was the 38th overall pick in the 2007 First-Year Player Draft, had a shot at making Toronto's Opening Day rotation during Spring Training.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes' no-decision against the Red Sox on Tuesday was an outing he'd like to forget. He had trouble commanding his pitches, particularly his curveball, and he was battered for seven runs on nine hits with a walk, a strikeout and a hit batter in just two-plus innings. Reyes had success working himself out of jams in previous outings, but his luck ran out in this one. He'll look to post his second victory of the season against the Blue Jays, to whom he allowed four runs on three hits with three walks and two strikeouts in six innings on April 12.

home_pitcher_note: Ortega settled in and pitched confidently in his second Major League start, holding the Yankees to four runs (three earned) across 6 1/3 innings at Yankee Stadium on Thursday night. He had two strikeouts and two walks while scattering eight hits, getting outs in key situations with his fastball finding good locations along with a quality curve and changeup. He has impressed the Angels with his poise as much as with his quality stuff, working out of trouble with confidence rare for a 23-year-old pitcher with so little experience.
away_pitcher_note:
On Friday against the Orioles, Halladay earned his fifth 
win of the season, giving up four runs (three earned) on 10 hits in eight innings. He threw 117 pitches, 80 of 
which were strikes, and walked only one batter while striking out six. Halladay's strikeout-to-walk ratio of 
8.00 is second in the American League behind Minnesota's Kevin Slowey (9.50). Over his career, Halladay 
is 6-5 against the Angels with an ERA of 4.63.
summary: 2009-05-06 - Toronto Blue Jays (13) @ Los Angeles Angels (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: After a frustrating first inning -- two full-count walks on close pitches, a single through the middle and Jorge Posada's two-run homer producing four runs -- Weaver settled in and pitched brilliantly, outdueling Andy Pettitte across six innings at Yankee Stadium on Friday night. It was the fourth high-caliber showing by Weaver in five starts, suggesting that he is returning to his dominant rookie form from 2006. The four earned runs raised his ERA from 2.45 to 3.13, but it was a much better performance than the numbers indicate. From the second through the sixth, he yielded two singles (one a bunt) and a walk. Weaver is 1-1 with a 6.35 ERA in two career starts against the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note:
Ray made his Major League debut against Baltimore on 
Saturday, going 5 2/3 innings and giving up three runs on three hits and four walks while striking out two. He earned a no-decision in a game the Jays eventually won, 5-4, in extra innings. Jays manager Cito Gaston had planned on keeping the young starter's pitch count below 100, and Ray ended up throwing 90 pitches, 56 of which were for strikes.
summary: 2009-05-07 - Toronto Blue Jays (1) @ Los Angeles Angels (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Outman turned in the best start of his young career, tossing six strong innings against the first-place Mariners. For the first time in his three 2009 starts, Outman only walked one batter, and his five strikeouts matched his total from his April 17 start in Toronto. Outman got through the six innings in 87 pitches, and 55 of those were thrown for strikes. The lefty's only hiccup came in the fourth inning, when Jose Lopez led off with a single and Mike Sweeney followed with a two-run home run to left field. Otherwise, Outman induced six ground-ball outs and three popups in his second Major League victory.
away_pitcher_note:
Richmond allowed three runs (two earned) on five 
hits and two walks against Baltimore at Rogers Centre on Sunday. He pitched seven innings, which 
matched a career high, throwing 99 pitches, 68 of which were for strikes. He has made one career start 
against Oakland (Aug. 5, 2008), earning a win while giving up three runs on seven hits in 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gallagher is making a spot start in place of rookie lefty Brett Anderson, who is being skipped after having to leave his past two starts with a bothersome blister on his left index finger. Upon taking over for Anderson on Monday, Gallagher, 23, worked 3 2/3 scoreless innings, giving up three hits without a walk while striking out three. Gallagher, who throws a mid-90s fastball, did not win a spot on the starting staff at Spring Training despite entering camp as a near lock and opened the year in the A's bullpen; he made three appearances before being optioned to Triple-A Sacramento to join the River Cats' rotation. He made two starts in the Minors and didn't allow a hit or a run over five innings while walking three and striking out seven. Obtained in the trade that sent Rich Harden and Chad Gaudin to the Cubs last summer, Gallagher made two starts against Toronto last season and lost both, allowing seven earned runs in a total of eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Tallet took a no-hitter into the seventh inning against the Indians on Monday before giving up a single to Ryan Garko with one out. He earned a no-decision in a game the Jays lost, 9-7, in 12 innings. He gave up three runs on four hits and three walks with five strikeouts in seven innings -- the longest outing of his career. Tallet threw a season-high 94 pitches in his fourth start since being moved from the bullpen to the rotation due to injuries to Toronto's starters.

home_pitcher_note: Braden, Oakland's Opening Night starter, has been the most consistent member of the rotation by a mile. He's worked at least six innings in four of his six starts and has three of the rotation's four wins. He wasn't at his best against the Angels on Tuesday, allowing three earned runs on eight hits and a walk over six innings, and given the run support he's gotten this year, he needs to be at his best to win. The A's have been shut out twice in his starts, and on Tuesday they scored once while he was in the game. One of those shutouts came on April 19, when Braden took the loss despite allowing one run on five hits over 7 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note:
Cecil, one of the Jays' top pitching prospects, made his 
Major League debut against Cleveland on Tuesday, going six strong innings and giving up two runs on six hits. Only one of the runs was earned, as Cleveland's Matt LaPorta scored on a fielding error by left fielder Travis Snider. Cecil hit three batters, but did not allow any walks and recorded six strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Toronto's ace was dominating in his last effort, reeling off eight strong innings in a road victory over the Angels on Wednesday. Halladay blanked Los Angeles for seven frames before allowing one run. The right-hander scattered six hits and ended with six strikeouts, two walks and 13 outs induced via ground balls. Halladay has six wins in seven starts, marking the fastest he has reached that many victories in a season in his career. In 32 games against New York in his career, Halladay has gone 15-5 with a 2.86 ERA. He went 5-1 with a 2.40 ERA against the Yankees last season.
away_pitcher_note: Assuming the Yankees don't alter their rotation with Monday's off-day, Burnett will face his former team for the first time this season. The right-hander is coming off Wednesday night's no-decision to Tampa Bay, in which Burnett allowed three runs over six innings. While not his best performance, Burnett did strike out eight Rays and was optimistic in his performance going forward.
summary: 2009-05-12 - New York Yankees (1) @ Toronto Blue Jays (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Richmond gave up more runs in one inning (five) in his last start than he has in any of his 10 previous starts. It doesn't mean the league has caught up to him though. After giving up five runs in the second inning of a 5-3 loss to Oakland on Friday, he pitched one-hit ball over the final six innings and recorded his first career complete game. This guy is a winner.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte is coming off a disappointing outing, in which he allowed a career-high four home runs and allowed five runs in six innings to the Rays. He did not factor in the decision in an eventual 8-6 Yankee loss. After not allowing more than three earned runs in any of his first four starts, Pettitte has now had two tough starts in a row. He surrendered five runs in 5 2/3 innings to the Angels on May 1.
summary: 2009-05-13 - New York Yankees (8) @ Toronto Blue Jays (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Tallet will make his regular start as the Blue Jays adjusted their rotation for the Yankees series. Robert Ray was pushed back to allow Tallet to make the start in the third game of the series with New York. It's a good choice. Tallet is coming off two consecutive overpowering starts. He completed a career-high seven innings in each of his last two starts and allowed four runs and six hits combined. He's throwing strikes and working quickly. Only one of his five starts thus far could be considered bad. In 20 relief appearances against the Yankees, he has a win, a hold and a 2.86 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia was in total control of the Orioles, hurling a complete-game four-hit shutout in his best performance as a Yankee to date. Sabathia had command of all his pitches and was locked in after Alex Rodriguez belted a three-run homer in the first inning, retiring 23 of 24 Orioles through one stretch. He walked one and struck out eight in the performance, hurling his 11th career complete-game shutout.
summary: 2009-05-14 - New York Yankees (3) @ Toronto Blue Jays (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: For a guy who was almost surprised to be called up, Cecil has shown maturity and calmness beyond his years. In 14 Major League innings, he has allowed one earned run, walked two and struck out 12. He threw eight shutout innings against the A's on Sunday, zeroing in on first-pitch strikes and leadoff outs. Cecil was never really in trouble and kept the ball down, inducing 12 ground-ball outs.
away_pitcher_note: Danks did not snap a two-game losing streak with his effort against the Rangers on Saturday night in Chicago, but as the old saying goes, he certainly pitched well enough to win. The left-hander set a career high with 10 strikeouts, giving up just one run on four hits, while walking one. Danks exited after 98 pitches and after working six innings, with the White Sox clinging to a 2-1 lead at the time. Texas rallied to tie the game in the seventh, leaving Danks with a no-decision. Danks has a 0-1 career record with a 2.79 ERA against the Blue Jays, with both career starts coming at the Rogers Centre.
summary: 2009-05-15 - Chicago White Sox (3) @ Toronto Blue Jays (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note:
Ray took his first loss in the second start of his Major 
League career in his last outing, which came on May 7 at Angel Stadium. He went a career-high 6 1/3 innings 
and gave up six runs (five earned) on 10 hits, including two home runs. His walk and strikeout totals 
showed improvement over his first start -- he struck out two batters and gave up four free passes in his 
Major League debut, but fanned four and walked none against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Colon started off strong during his first career Mother's Day start, allowing one run on Hank Blalock's solo home run over four innings, but the burly right-hander didn't get out of the fifth, giving up four runs on four hits. Colon struck out four and walked three, but he threw only 52 of his 93 pitches for strikes. The loss on Sunday ended a personal 12-game winning streak Colon had over the Rangers. Colon, whose career record slipped to 152-100 on Sunday, has an 8-3 record and 3.80 ERA against the Blue Jays to go with his 4-2 career record at Rogers Centre.
summary: 2009-05-16 - Chicago White Sox (1) @ Toronto Blue Jays (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note:
Halladay threw his first complete game of the year 
against the Yankees at Rogers Centre on Tuesday. He gave up one run on five hits -- matching his lowest 
total this season -- and struck out five. For the third time in his eight starts this year, he did not walk a 
single batter. He got 16 outs via ground ball, and gave up only two extra base hits, both doubles.
away_pitcher_note: For the fourth time in seven trips to the mound, Floyd failed to post a coveted quality start. Monday's start against the Indians was actually well below the quality cut-off, as the right-hander gave up eight runs on 11 hits over five-plus innings, including two batters faced in the sixth. Floyd has a 0-2 record with a 9.74 ERA in his past four starts and has allowed more double-digit-hit games this season (two) then he did in all of 2008. Floyd already has a 0-1 record with a 10.38 ERA against the Blue Jays this year and stands at 0-2 lifetime against the Blue Jays. But Floyd has never worked at Rogers Centre.
summary: 2009-05-17 - Chicago White Sox (2) @ Toronto Blue Jays (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Richmond gave up five runs to the Yankees, all in the second inning, on Wednesday at Rogers Centre. He lasted only 1 2/3 innings, giving up seven hits and two walks on his way to his second loss of the season. Five of the hits he gave up were for extra bases, including a home run and two triples, all in the second inning. He struck out two batters -- the first two he faced at the top of the first. Of the 58 pitches he threw, 31 were strikes. It was the second game in a row Richmond has given up five runs in the second inning. He has never faced the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Richard did not exactly dominate against the Indians at Progressive Field, but he certainly did well enough to earn another start in manager Ozzie Guillen's mind. Richard allowed four runs on six hits over 3 1/3 innings, with Guillen trying to stretch the southpaw a little beyond his limit, at 79 pitches, in order to get him ready for his next trip to the mound. Richard struck out two and walked three. He gave up two runs in three innings of relief earlier this season against the Blue Jays and has a 0-1 record lifetime against the Blue Jays. Richard has never pitched at Rogers Centre.
summary: 2009-05-18 - Chicago White Sox (2) @ Toronto Blue Jays (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Uncharacteristically, the veteran knuckleballer squandered an early 4-0 lead in his last start, which was easily his worst of the season. Wakefield was belted around for 11 hits and seven runs over 4 2/3 innings. This will be Wakefield's third start of the season at Fenway, where he is 2-0 with a 2.08 ERA. Wakefield is 16-11 lifetime against the Blue Jays with a 3.76 ERA.
away_pitcher_note:
Tallet recorded a no-decision on Thursday against the 
Yankees at Rogers Centre. He went six-plus innings, giving up two runs on four hits and five walks. He 
walked Yankees right fielder Nick Swisher with the bases loaded in the first inning, but settled down after 
that, giving up only two singles and a walk in the second through sixth innings. He left the game with 
runners on the corners with no outs in the seventh inning, and was charged with a run when New York's 
Brett Gardner, who Tallet left on third, scored.
summary: 2009-05-19 - Toronto Blue Jays (1) @ Boston Red Sox (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The big righty was unspectacular in his last start, giving up seven hits and four runs over 6 1/3 innings. He walked one and struck out four in a no-decision. The Red Sox lost the game in 12 innings. Overall, Penny seems to be settling into a better rhythm than he was in earlier on the season. He has gone six innings or more in his past three starts. This will be Penny's fourth start of the season at Fenway, where he is 2-0 with a 7.63 ERA.
away_pitcher_note:
Cecil won at home for the first time in his career as the 
Blue Jays defeated the White Sox on Friday at Rogers Centre. Cecil gave up three runs in six innings and 
has now recorded three consecutive quality starts to open his Major League career. He allowed six hits and 
two walks against Chicago and struck out three. The three runs he gave up came via two home runs. Cecil 
has never faced the Red Sox.
summary: 2009-05-20 - Toronto Blue Jays (3) @ Boston Red Sox (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lester was in control of his last start against Seattle until the sixth inning, when he lost a three-run lead by giving up a two-run single and a two-run homer to Ichiro Suzuki, the Mariners right fielder's second homer in the game off the left-hander. Lester has now given up at least one home run in each of his last four starts and has allowed two long balls in three of those outings. He has given up 13 runs on 18 hits in his last 10 innings pitched.
away_pitcher_note:
Ray recorded his first Major League win on Saturday, as 
the Jays defeated the White Sox, 2-1, at Rogers Centre. He went a career-high eight innings, allowing three 
hits -- the fewest he has given up in his three big league starts -- and issuing one walk. The only run he 
allowed was unearned, as Chicago's Scott Podsednik stole third base and scored on a throwing error by 
Jays catcher Raul Chavez. Ray struck out three and did not allow any extra-base hits.
summary: 2009-05-21 - Toronto Blue Jays (1) @ Boston Red Sox (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kawakami had a solid outing Saturday night against the Diamondbacks, but was saddled with the loss as Atlanta lost, 12-0, at Turner Field. The Japanese right-hander went five innings while giving up three runs on five hits. After struggling early, he retired the last eight men he faced. Kawakami has had command issues this season, averaging five walks per nine innings. Although he only walked one batter against the D-Backs, the 33-year-old rookie was burned by four extra-base hits. This will be his first career start against the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday against the White Sox at Rogers Centre, Halladay allowed two runs in seven innings for his eighth win of the season. Only one of the runs was earned, as Halladay committed a fielding error that allowed Chicago second baseman Chris Getz to get on base, and Getz eventually came around to score. Both runs were scored in the first inning. Halladay allowed six hits and one walk, striking out eight. He pounded the strike zone, throwing 77 of his 103 pitches for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Grasping his role as the Braves ace, Lowe has pitched at least seven innings and allowed less than three runs in four of his past five starts.  While limiting the Rockies to two runs and three hits in eight innings on Monday night, the 35-year-old right-hander lost his bid to win five consecutive starts. Lowe is 3-4 with a 4.94 ERA in nine career starts against the Blue Jays. But he's 1-1 with a 2.49 ERA in his past three outings against them.
away_pitcher_note: Janssen has been waiting a long time for this start. The 27-year-old right-hander missed the entire 2008 season after undergoing surgery on his right shoulder, and an unrelated shoulder issue cost him a chance of making Toronto's Opening Day roster during Spring Training. In five starts in the Minors this year, Janssen posted a 0.76 ERA between stints with Class A Dunedin and Double-A New Hampshire. Janssen last pitched in the Majors in 2007, when he posted a 2.35 ERA in 70 games as a setup man for the Jays.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens of late has been nothing short of unhittable for the Braves. The 23-year-old right-hander improved to 4-2 and lowered his ERA below 2.00 with another quality start against the Rockies on Tuesday. "Baseball's a beautiful game." Moyer needs two more wins to tie Carl Hubbell (253) for 42nd place on the all-time list.

Despite a 37-pitch third frame, Richmond settled down from there and did not allow a single base runner after that inning.
away_pitcher_note: Garza got back on track against the Phillies Wednesday after suffering three losses in his last three decisions. The 25-year-old right-hander allowed one run on three hits while walking four and striking out seven in eight innings to earn his fifth win of the season. Garza has the best stuff on the staff and seems to be maturing on the mound, where he has experienced problems controlling his emotions in the past. Garza is 3-3 with a 1.99 ERA in six career starts against the Blue Jays; he is 1-2 with a 0.79 ERA in three career starts at Rogers Centre.
summary: 2009-06-30 - Tampa Bay Rays (4) @ Toronto Blue Jays (1) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: Romero continues to impress in his first season in the big leagues, picking up a win over the Yankees on Monday in New York. Rzepczynski's walks came back to bite him, though. He issues three in the fourth inning, including one to force home a costly run.

summary: 2009-07-18 - Boston Red Sox (2) @ Toronto Blue Jays (6) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: After five straight tough-luck losses, Lee finally won a game on Thursday. Lee had great command and relied on great defense to get his fifth win of the season. He is 1-4 with a 4.37 ERA in eight starts in his career against Toronto.

The rookie's eight strikeouts fell one shy of his season high, but he struggled with his command, issuing five walks -- tied for the most he's allowed all season. So he should be ready to go when he makes his first start of the second half against the Blue Jays Wednesday. He is 2-3 with a 5.45 ERA in seven career starts against Toronto.

away_pitcher_note: Huff is continuing to learn on the job. He pitched well on Friday against the Mariners but couldn't keep his pitch count down and forced the Indians to go to their bullpen early. It was the seventh game this season (including an injury-shortened three-inning start) in which Halladay did not issue a single walk. He received a no-decision his last time out against the Royals after allowing three runs in five innings. He needs to find a way to harness his stuff since on many occasions it is so electric that it misses the strike zone. Sunday he walked five -- including one with the bases loaded. Garza has done well against the Blue Jays in his career. He is 4-3 with a 1.89 ERA in seven career starts against them and 2-2 with a 0.91 ERA in four career starts in Toronto.

summary: 2009-07-25 - Tampa Bay Rays (10) @ Toronto Blue Jays (9) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: The 6-foot-9, 280-pound Niemann dazzled once again in a 3-2 victory against the White Sox on Tuesday. Rays manager Joe Maddon said that, including Tuesday's performance, the three best games thrown by a Rays pitcher this year all belonged to Niemann, who also has tossed two complete-game shutouts. With the victory, Niemann's ninth this season, he tied for the most among American League rookies with Detroit's Rick Porcello. summary: 2009-07-26 - Tampa Bay Rays (1) @ Toronto Blue Jays (5) (Final)

This is his first start against Toronto this season, but he is 2-1 with a 2.89 ERA in four career starts against the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Romero won his first game in four starts in a 10-6 victory over the Indians on Wednesday at Rogers Centre. He gave up four runs (all earned) on four hits, lasting 5 1/3 innings. He struggled with his command, issuing five walks, which tied a season high. He had only two strikeouts -- tied for the fewest in any start this season. home_pitcher_note: Washburn has pitched like a Cy Young candidate over his last seven starts. Last time out, he got the win against the Tigers by throwing seven scoreless innings and allowing just two hits. This will be his first start against the Blue Jays this season, and he's 4-7 lifetime against Toronto with a 4.23 ERA. Washburn hasn't lost since July 1.
away_pitcher_note: Rzepczynski did not record a quality start for the first time in his four Major League starts, taking the loss as the Indians beat the Jays, 5-4, on Thursday at Rogers Centre. In his shortest start this year, Rzepczynski gave up four runs on three hits in 4 1/3 innings. Only two of the runs were earned, as a fielding error by third baseman Jose Bautista led to a pair of unearned runs in the fifth inning. Rzepczynski issued four walks, hit a batter and struck out six. He has never faced the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith made his first start after a long rehab stint with Triple-A Tacoma, against the Indians, and he didn't disappoint. Things got away from him a little bit in the seventh inning when he gave up two home runs, and he ended up allowing four runs over seven innings in the M's 9-0 loss. But he retired 14 batters in a row at one point, and said his curveball felt particularly sharp. The left-hander has made three career appearances against Toronto, and is 0-0 with a 5.63 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay pitched nine innings for the fourth time this season, allowing only two runs, but came away with a no-decision in a 10-inning, 4-2 loss to the Rays on Friday at Rogers Centre. One of the two runs was unearned due to a third-inning passed ball by catcher Rod Barajas. Halladay allowed four hits and issued three walks. He struck out 10, marking the second time this year he has fanned 10 or more batters. Halladay has not faced Seattle this year, but is 5-4 with a 2.67 ERA in 11 career starts (13 appearances) against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Twice handed leads early in last Sunday's game at Yankee Stadium, Braden twice surrendered them and was fuming afterward because it continued a trend. He'd done the same thing in his previous start, a loss to the Twins in Oakland. The trend marks a pretty dramatic reversal for Braden, who spent the first three months of the season pitching like an ace but rarely had anything to show for it because his run support was among the worst in the American League. To wit, Braden on April 19 held the host Blue Jays to one run on five hits over 7 1/3 innings but was tagged with a 1-0 loss, and on May 10 in Oakland he posted another quality start againt Toronto but took a 5-0 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Richmond will likely return from the disabled list (shoulder) to make his 14th start of the season. He hasn't pitched since June 30, when he took the loss after allowing three runs over seven innings against Tampa Bay. Richmond gives the Jays another option to balance out their trio of young pitchers, and could be a key addition to the rotation if Roy Halladay is traded before the non-waiver Trade Deadline. He's faced Oakland once this year, an eight-inning effort that resulted in a loss after he allowed five runs on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill, who'd been outstanding in a victory over the Twins his previous time out, struggled against the host Red Sox in the opener of a four-game series on Monday, allowing six runs on 10 hits and two walks over five innings while absorbing his fourth loss in five decisions. A sinkerball specialist who need to keep his money pitch below opponents' knees to success, Cahill set the tone for his disappointing outing by surrendering a solo homer to Dustin Pedroia on a thigh-high fastball in the bottom of the first inning. Cahill has faced the Blue Jays once this year, allowing two runs on five hits and five walks over 5 1/3 innings on the way to a no-decision in Toronto on April 18.
away_pitcher_note: Cecil has been on a nice run ever since allowing seven runs in 3 2/3 innings in a start against the Yankees on July 5. In the three outings since that forgettable performance, the young lefty has gone 2-0 with a 0.45 ERA, striking out 21 and walking nine over 20 innings. On Sunday, Cecil picked up a win at home against the Rays after allowing one run on four hits with seven strikeouts and three walks over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Mazzaro, a 22-year-old rookie, won the first two starts of his career but is winless in nine subsequent assignments, and it took a game-tying, three-run rally in the ninth inning Tuesday to prevent him from becoming the first A's starter to lose seven consecutive starts since Brian Kingman lost nine in a row in 1980. Mazzaro, who dominates when he keeps his fastball below the knees or above the belt, again struggled with location his last time out and gave up five runs in the third inning against the host Red Sox. In all, he was was charged with six runs on nine hits and two walks while striking out three over six innings. Mazzaro has never faced the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Romero wasn't real sharp in his last outing against the Mariners, but he managed to give a solid six innings in an 11-4 win. The lefty gave up four runs and 10 hits, but said he was happy with the way he attacked the strike zone and pitched to contact. Romero has been a reliable arm for the Jays all season, and his 11 quality starts are the second-most in the Majors for a rookie. He's never faced the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay, whose name was included in countless rumors last month, survived Friday's Trade Deadline and remains the ace of Toronto's rotation. away_pitcher_note: When Marcum takes the mound for the Blue Jays on Opening Day, it will be significant for a couple of reasons. For Toronto, it will mark the first time since 2002 that a pitcher other than Roy Halladay takes the mound for the season opener, ending a seven-year streak. For Marcum, the outing will represent his first Major League start for the Jays since Sept. 16, 2008. Following that season, the starter underwent Tommy John surgery on his right elbow. Healthy and back at full strength, Marcum enters this season as the Jays' new No. 1 starter, filling the spot vacated when Halladay was traded to the Phillies in December. Marcum earned the top slot due to his experience (64 career starts) and his track record as a starter (23-15 with a 3.85 ERA). Marcum's strength is keeping hitters off-balance, especially with his two changeups -- one to mimic his four-seam fastball and another that looks like his cutter. The 28-year-old righty won't overpower hitters, but when his location is sharp and he has his offspeed offerings working, Marcum has the potential to be a great leader for Toronto's relatively young pitching staff.

home_pitcher_note: Harden was signed by the Rangers as a free agent in the offseason after spending 2009 with the Cubs. Since 2003, he has struck out 9.35 batters per nine innings, the highest of any Major League pitcher with at least 125 starts. away_pitcher_note: A year ago, Tallet began the season as he usually did for the Blue Jays -- in their bullpen. Before the end of April, Toronto asked the veteran left-hander to shift into the rotation in the wake of injuries. Tallet obliged and went on to make a career-high 25 starts, going 7-8 with a 5.41 ERA as a starter for the Jays. After spending the bulk of his big league career as a reliever, Tallet loved the chance to return to the job he prefers. This spring, with a relatively young and inexperienced rotation, the Jays gave Tallet the opportunity to earn a spot on the starting staff again. Toronto ultimately handed the 32-year-old Tallet the No. 2 role due to his experience in the Majors.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson joins the rotation after four years as a reliever. Wilson pitches more as a starter and relies on excellent location rather than trying to blow hitters away with perfect pitches as a late-innings reliever. away_pitcher_note: It took Romero until the final few days of Spring Training to convince the Jays to hand him a rotation spot for the 2009 season. Over his first 12 starts last year, Romero went 7-3 with a 2.96 ERA and was an early favorite for the American League Rookie of the Year honor. The lefty went 6-6 with a 5.36 ERA over his final 17 turns, though, taking him out of the running for the annual award. This spring, Romero concentrated on limiting his walks and continued to develop his sinker. Romero was considered for the Opening Day starter role, but Toronto ultimately decided to hand that honor to the more experienced Shaun Marcum.

The right-hander was pretty much caught up to the rest of the rotation midway through camp and will look to build on a successful 2009. away_pitcher_note: The fact that Eveland is out of player options helped his cause when it came to competing for a spot on the Opening Day roster.
