home_pitcher_note: Statistically Morrow has looked like a different pitcher in his past two starts, giving up only two earned runs over 13 innings, while recording 16 strikeouts over that span. That being said, Morrow still displayed some of the control issues that have plagued him in the past. Against the Rays on Sunday, Morrow walked six batters over six innings and was bailed out on several occasions by catcher Jose Molina, who threw out a career-high four baserunners. It is imperative that Morrow maintain his high strikeout rate; on several occasions against the Rays he was able to prevent a potential big inning by stranding baserunners. Morrow is 2-0 against the Athletics with a 4.13 ERA over 32 2/3 career innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill will make his season debut Friday in place of lefty Brett Anderson, who suffered a strain near his flexor tendon and was placed on the 15-day disabled list this week. The 22-year-old Cahill began the season on the DL with a left scapula stress reaction before being activated April 20 and immediately sent to Triple-A Sacramento, where he was 1-0 with a 1.04 ERA in two starts. The A's righty spent the entire 2009 season in the A's starting rotation en route to posting a 10-13 record with a 4.63 ERA. He joined Anderson in making the jump from Double-A Midland to the big leagues, where he made 32 starts and compiled 178 2/3 innings. In two career starts against Toronto, Cahill is 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA. He surrendered 13 hits and eight runs in a combined 10 2/3 innings vs. the Blue Jays last season.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland fell back down to earth in his last start against Boston on Monday, giving up seven earned runs in just three innings as the Blue Jays fell to the Red Sox, 13-12. Somehow, Eveland managed to escape without the loss as Red Sox ace Josh Beckett blew a five-run lead and was yanked after just three-plus innings. Going into that contest, Eveland spotted a dazzling 1.93 ERA, but left with an ERA of 4.57 -- what a difference a night can make. Eveland's next outing will come against his former club, the Oakland Athletics, whom he's never faced.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez tossed what was arguably his finest performance of the season thus far -- a seven-inning shutout performance against the Indians, who garnered just five hits off the A's lefty. The seven innings pitched tied a career high, and Gonzalez also struck out three in the winning effort. He had walked a combined 10 batters in his previous three starts, but Gonzalez offered up just two free passes in the outing. After the game, A's manager Bob Geren mentioned Gonzalez had remarkable life on his fastball and used his always impressive breaking ball often while mixing in a few changeups to offset his other two pitches. In his lone career start against the Blue Jays in 2008, Gonzalez gave up four runs on four hits and two walks in a loss.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum can't do much more to earn a win. He's already had four quality starts in five outings and has pitched at least seven innings in all but one appearance. On Tuesday night against the Red Sox, it was a familiar scene as the Blue Jays' bullpen collapsed and walked across the winning run in a 2-1 loss. Marcum went seven innings, allowing only one run in the losing effort. While Marcum has made it clear that wins are something he can't entirely control, he has not won a game since April 11, 2008 -- prior to undergoing Tommy John surgery. Marcum is 1-1 lifetime against the Athletics, with a 4.15 ERA over 21 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets had his shortest outing of the year in his last start, against the Rays, surrendering eight earned runs on nine hits and a walk with two strikeouts. The righty served up a pair of home runs after allowing just one over his first four starts combined. Sheets made no excuses for his rather forgettable performance and will look to bounce back vs. a Blue Jays team against which he owns a 2-0 record and 1.93 ERA in two career starts. The last time Sheets faced Toronto was two years ago, when he offered up two runs, four hits and four walks in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Talbot has been surprisingly stingy with the runs allowed this season. Plenty of balls get put in play against him, but he's done an excellent job limiting the damage on the scoreboard. Talbot has now notched three straight quality starts, allowing just two earned runs over 21 1/3 innings. In his last start against the Angels on Tuesday, he went 6 1/3 innings, allowing just a run on six hits with three walks and a strikeout. He got into a couple jams but was able to work his way out of them, thanks to his deep arsenal. To put it simply, the Indians are getting great value out of their fifth starter, who was the player to be named in the Kelly Shoppach trade with the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Despite losing, Cecil was simply outstanding in his last outing. He was limited to osix innings and 100 pitches, but the left-hander did all he could, surrendering only one run on five hits against a tough Boston lineup. The only run he allowed was on a Dustin Pedroia sacrifice fly in his last inning. Most impressive so far may be Cecil's ability to limit walks (two in 12 2/3 innings) and to throw strikes (62 percent of his pitches). The sophomore has limited Cleveland to one run in 13 career innings.

home_pitcher_note: It could be a product of missing nearly two years because of Tommy John elbow surgery, but Westbrook has had issues with endurance. His last start, against the Angels on Wednesday, was a prime example. Westbrook cruised for the better part of his first five innings, but he lost effectiveness in the sixth. He let the first two men of the inning aboard, then served up a game-tying, three-run homer to Torii Hunter, thereby saddling himself with no decision. Westbrook hasn't notched a Major League win since April 8, 2008. This will be his first start against Toronto since May 2, 2007.
away_pitcher_note: While Romero was not spectacular in his last outing vs. the A's on Wednesday, giving up three runs on four hits and four walks through six innings, he was still able to record his fifth straight quality start on his way to a 6-3 win. Romero was particularly happy with his outing, citing his ability to battle without his best stuff. The young left-hander will look to continue his success against the Indians, whom he has delivered a 1-0 record with a 2.25 ERA over eight career innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona followed up his strongest start of the season with his least effective. Whereas he dominated the A's for 7 1/3 innings in Oakland on April 24, he labored in six innings against the Twins on Friday. He allowed six runs on eight hits with two walks, a wild pitch and two strikeouts. He was less efficient than he had been in previous outings, needing 102 pitches to get through the six innings. While the outing wasn't an outright disaster, it was a step back for Carmona, who had been steadily improving with each previous start in April.
away_pitcher_note: This season has been a tale of two Morrows. Through his first two starts of the season, Morrow surrendered 12 runs on 12 hits over nine innings. Through his past three starts, Morrow has pitched 19 innings and allowed only five runs while striking out 25. Morrow has even said that he feels more comfortable working out of the stretch this season, where he has been able to escape several jams via the strikeout. Morrow, who was plagued by the home run in his first two starts (three), has not given up a long ball over his past three outings, a sign of increased control. The right-hander has never started a game vs. the Indians, but is 1-1 with a 4.26 ERA in a relief role.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander showed his increasing mound confidence and veteran grit by battling through Saturday afternoon's balmy conditions at Yankee Stadium without his best stuff. The left-hander exited after five innings, allowing two runs on six hits over five innings, but elevating his pitch count to a season-high 118 pitches. Danks has limited opponents to two earned runs or fewer in each of his first five starts. According to Elias Sports Bureau, the last White Sox pitcher to accomplish the feat was Jose Contreras, who did so in his first six starts of 2006. Danks gave up one run over seven innings during a victory over the Blue Jays earlier this season at Rogers Centre, and has a career record of 1-2 against Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland labored through his last start vs. the A's on Saturday, giving up four earned runs on eight hits and three walks over 6 2/3 innings. Really the only significant blemish was a two-run home run to shortstop Cliff Pennington in the fourth. After that, Eveland settled down and cruised through his remaining 2 2/3 innings, before being replaced by lefty Scott Downs. It appears Eveland's 1.93 ERA through his first three starts may have been a facade, but give the big left-hander credit for bouncing back late in his last outing. Against the Indians, Eveland is 2-0 lifetime with a 1.50 ERA in 12 innings.
summary: 2010-05-06 - Toronto Blue Jays (2) @ Chicago White Sox (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle's recent struggles continued, as he lost his fourth straight decision overall on Sunday afternoon at Yankee Stadium. The left-hander was victimized by home runs from Brett Gardner and Robinson Cano, both left-handed hitters, and allowed five runs on 10 hits over 4 2/3 innings. He struck out three and walked one, while throwing 93 pitches. Buehrle has given up 18 earned runs on 32 hits over 22 1/3 innings during this four-game skid. While Buehrle slipped to 1-7 lifetime against the Yankees, he brings a 5-3 career record against the Blue Jays into Friday's start and a 78-47 mark at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum's run of tough luck ended with his last start, in which he earned his first win since September 11, 2008, against the White Sox. Marcum, who missed last season recovering from Tommy John surgery, went 6 1/3 innings against the A's, allowing a run on six hits and four walks. Marcum fanned six Oakland batters. In his previous five starts in 2010, Marcum had given up more than three runs only one time yet had nothing to show for it in the win column. The last time Marcum faced the Pale Hose, he gave up two runs in 7 1/3 innings on five hits and a walk, striking out six.
summary: 2010-05-07 - Toronto Blue Jays (7) @ Chicago White Sox (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The Peavy who was on the mound during Monday's series-opening victory over the Royals is the Peavy whom the White Sox expect to be  the ace of their staff for this season and beyond. Peavy gave up just four hits over seven scoreless innings, and fanned a season-high nine. Of greater importance was that he only walked one, after issuing 20 free passes during the month of April. Peavy made his only career start against Toronto earlier this season at Rogers Centre and did not factor in the decision after allowing seven runs on eight hits over 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cecil took a perfect game into the seventh inning in his last start, shutting down the Indians on the first game of the current road trip. Cecil's dominance set the tone in Toronto's 5-1 victory. Jhonny Peralta's RBI single in the seventh inning was the lone hit Cecil allowed in the eight innings he pitched and it scored the Tribe's lone run. Cecil walked two Indians batters and struck out 10. Cecil has faced the White Sox once, beating them on May 5, 2009. Chicago tagged Cecil for three runs on six hits and a pair of walks, and the lefty fanned two.
summary: 2010-05-08 - Toronto Blue Jays (3) @ Chicago White Sox (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The tightrope walked by Gavin Floyd during the first three innings of Tuesday's game against Kansas City finally went out from under him in the seventh inning of a 7-2 loss. The Royals put 10 runners on base against Floyd over those first three frames but scored only two runs. In the seventh, the Royals knocked out four straight hits during a four-run rally that ran the right-hander from the game. Floyd finished with six runs allowed on a career-worst 13 hits. Through 32 2/3 innings, Floyd has yielded 45 hits and issued 14 walks. He has a 0-1 record against the Blue Jays in 2010, having given up four runs on nine hits over six innings in Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: Romero started strong against the Indians in his last outing, fanning five of the first six batters he faced. The lefty had to buckle down for the rest of his six innings, but he picked up his third win of the season, giving up five runs on nine hits and two walks. Romero finished with nine strikeouts against the Tribe but struggled with control, making three wild pitches and pushing his season total to 10. The last time Romero faced the White Sox, he made his signature outing of the young 2010 season, compiling 12 strikeouts and giving up two runs on a hit and two walks over eight innings.
summary: 2010-05-09 - Toronto Blue Jays (9) @ Chicago White Sox (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The big righty is coming off a tremendous performance against his former team, the Angels. In that one, Lackey gave up two hits and a run over seven innings. He walked two and struck out four. The righty has given up two earned runs or less in five of his six starts. Opponents are hitting Lackey at a .272 clip. He is 2-1 with a 4.63 ERA in four Fenway starts. Lifetime against the Jays, Lackey is 3-3 with a 3.31 ERA. In May, Lackey has a career record of 14-12 with a 3.69 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Morrow wasn't spectacular in his last outing vs. Cleveland, surrendering three runs on six hits and four walks over 5 1/3 innings, but he pitched well enough to keep his team in the game, as the Blue Jays went on to stage a late comeback in the ninth and take the game, 5-4. In all but one start this season, Morrow has failed to pitch beyond the sixth inning. He has racked up high pitch counts early in ballgames due to his heavy reliance on strikeouts -- he has eight or more in his past four starts. Wednesday in Cleveland also marked the first time Morrow has allowed a home run since his second start of the season against the White Sox -- a 22-inning stretch. Morrow boasts a lifetime 3.60 ERA against the Red Sox over 15 innings.
summary: 2010-05-10 - Toronto Blue Jays (6) @ Boston Red Sox (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In his first two starts since coming off the disabled list, Matsuzaka has been victimized by one bad inning. He gave up four runs in the first inning in his last start but bounced back well enough to earn the win. In that one, Dice-K gave up five hits and five runs over 5 1/3 innings. He walked three and struck out three, throwing 92 pitches. His first start was the complete opposite, as Matsuzaka was brilliant over his first four innings and then allowed six runs in the fifth. In 37 career starts at Fenway, Matsuzaka is 20-11 with a 4.47 ERA. Lifetime against the Blue Jays, he is 7-4 with a 3.86 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland outdueled fellow left-hander John Danks on Thursday, as the Blue Jays went on to defeat the White Sox, 2-0. Eveland went seven innings, allowing only two hits while tossing in three strikeouts. It was encouraging for Eveland to get back into the win column, as he struggled in his previous two outings -- eleven runs over 9 2/3 frames.  Eveland's season has been a rollercoaster thus far, but it's hard to complain with his 3-1 record and 3.82 ERA. The Red Sox have had Eveland's number over his career, as he is 0-2 with a 18.24 ERA over 12 1/3 frames.
summary: 2010-05-11 - Toronto Blue Jays (1) @ Boston Red Sox (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wakefield's last start was April 25 against Baltimore, after which he was subsequently moved to the bullpen to make room in the rotation for Daisuke Matsuzaka. On May 1, Wakefield made his first relief appearance since June 9, 2004, throwing 2 1/3 innings in the Red Sox's 12-9 loss in Baltimore. Between relief appearances he had made 162 starts. On Wednesday he will return to the rotation, albeit temporarily, to face the Blue Jays at Fenway Park, pushing Josh Beckett's next start to Friday in Detroit. As a starter this season, Wakefield is 0-1 with a 5.40 ERA. In three relief appearances, spanning 6 1/3 innings, he has given up six earned runs on seven hits, with no walks and two strikeouts, for an ERA of 8.53.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum contributed his fourth straight quality start for the Blue Jays on Friday against the White Sox but once again failed to earn a victory, as the club staged a late extra-innings rally to win, 7-4. The right-hander went 7 2/3 innings, allowing three runs on six hits without issuing a walk. He did however, double his season's home run total as both Mark Kotsay and Alex Rios went deep. Aside from the two home runs, it was vintage Marcum, who was economical with his pitches, utilizing his outstanding changeup to keep hitters off balance. Marcum has been fantastic against the Red Sox throughout his career, showcasing a  4-2 record with a 3.33 ERA over 48 2/3 innings.
summary: 2010-05-12 - Toronto Blue Jays (3) @ Boston Red Sox (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: While Cecil wasn't as dominant as his eight-inning, 10-strikeout performance against the Indians two starts ago, he pitched serviceably against the White Sox on Saturday in a 7-3 Blue Jays loss. Cecil went 5 1/3, allowing three runs on seven hits, chipping in three strikeouts. The bulk of the damage came in the first inning courtesy a two-out, two-run blast by White Sox slugger Paul Konerko. After a bases-loaded walk to Gordon Beckham in the second inning, Cecil settled down and cruised through his final 3 1/3 frames until being removed in the sixth because of a high pitch count (105). Credit the White Sox for battling as they forced Cecil to throw 61 of his pitches over the first two innings, contributing to his early exit. Over four starts Cecil's ERA sits at 3.12 with an impressive 24:7 strikeout-to-walk ratio. Cecil will pitch at home for only the second time this season, welcoming the Rangers, against whom he is 1-0 lifetime with a 12.60 ERA over one start -- an 18-10 Blue Jays victory.
away_pitcher_note: Harden allowed two runs in five innings in his last start against the Royals on Saturday. He didn't get the victory, but the Rangers ended up winning, 3-2. He is 2-0 with a 2.82 ERA in his last four games and the Rangers have won all four. He has struck out 34 and walked 25 in 35 2/3 innings, while opponents are hitting .225 off him. They are hitting .206 off him with runners in scoring position. He is 1-1 with a 3.24 ERA in three starts on the road. Harden, who is from Canada, is 0-3 with a 4.54 ERA in seven starts against the Blue Jays and 0-2 with a 10.61 ERA in two starts in Toronto.

home_pitcher_note: Romero was not his usual self against the White Sox on Sunday, lasting only 5 1/3 while surrendering four runs on eight hits with five walks. Although the Jays went on to win the game, 9-7, the five walks by Romero marked a season high. His lack of control was also evidenced by two wild pitches, bringing his season total to 12 -- he threw six all of last year. On the positive side, Romero has not been tagged for a home run since Tampa Bay's Jason Bartlett took him deep 20 1/3 innings ago. Romero also managed to fan seven White Sox, bringing his strikeout total to 22 over his past three starts. Look for a rebound at home against the Rangers. The young left-hander has dominated Texas in the past with a 1.35 ERA over 13 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman has gone five starts without getting a win. He managed to make it through just four innings on Sunday afternoon, allowing four runs on six hits and two walks in the Rangers' 6-4 victory over the Royals and was pulled after throwing 100 pitches. Feldman is 0-3 with a 7.83 ERA in his last five starts since going seven innings in a 9-2 victory over the Mariners on April 11. He is 0-2 with a 10.61 ERA in two road starts after winning a club-record 12 games on the road last year. Left-handed hitters are batting .319 off him. He is 0-2 with a 5.90 ERA in four starts and three relief appearances against the Blue Jays.

home_pitcher_note: Morrow was dominant over his past four starts -- 2.96 ERA with 34 strikeouts -- heading into Monday's contest against the Red Sox, but was nothing short of awful at Fenway Park, going only 1 2/3 innings as Boston torched him for six runs, resulting in a 7-6 Blue Jays loss. Morrow set a Toronto record for most walks issued in an inning, with five, leading to a four-run second inning and the early hook from manager Cito Gaston. Blue Jays fans can only hope that this start was an anomaly, but Morrow certainly looked like the same pitcher who started the season with significant control problems and an ERA of 12.00 through his first two starts. Morrow has been lackluster in his career vs. Texas, going 2-4 with a 4.94 ERA over 23 2/3 frames.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis is 0-1 with a 2.45 ERA in his last three starts. He allowed three runs in seven innings in his last start against the Athletics on Tuesday and was not involved in the decision. The Rangers ended up losing in 13 innings. He is 1-1 with a 2.84 ERA in four starts on the road. Opponents are hitting .202 off him, including .176 by right-handed batters. They are 3-for-35 off him with runners in scoring position. In 45 2/3 innings he has struck out 49 and walked 17. He is 1-2 with a 12.08 ERA in his career against the Blue Jays. That's his highest ERA against any American League team.

home_pitcher_note:
After a strong start to the season, Eveland 
has hit a bit of a lull out of the back end of the Blue Jays' rotation. Over his past four outings, the finesse left-hander has gone 1-2 with a 7.40 ERA. The lone victory during that stretch came after Eveland logged seven shutout innings against the White Sox on May 6. One start later, the lefty surrendered six runs on six hits over four innings, during which he walked four and fired off 102 pitches. Eveland will aim to return to the form that he displayed against Chicago and over his first three appearances of the season. Out of the gates, he went 2-0 with a 1.93 ERA in three turns. Eveland has posted a 1.80 ERA in three career games against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: A trend has developed for Slowey so far this season and it's been his inability to pitch deep into outings. The right-hander had an eight-inning gem against the Indians on April 20 at Target Field, but it's the only one of his seven starts in which he has pitched past the sixth inning. Early on in Slowey's last start against the White Sox, it looked like he might be turning things around. Slowey needed just 39 pitches to get through four innings, but he threw 36 pitches while facing nine batters in the fifth as he couldn't even finish the frame. Slowey gave up five runs -- all in that fifth inning -- as he lasted just 4 2/3 innings against Chicago to pick up his third loss of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum only received three runs of support in his last outing, but that proved to be enough for the right-hander to avoid another no-decision or a hard-luck loss. On Wednesday in Boston, Marcum held the Red Sox to no runs on just two hits across seven sharp innings. He struck out six and walked just one. Over his past five starts, Toronto's No. 1 arm has fashioned a 2-0 record to go along with a tidy 2.06 ERA. Dating back to the start of the 2007 season, Marcum has opened an outing with at least six shutout frames. In his career against Minnesota, Marcum has gone 1-1 with a 4.26 ERA over three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano's record certainly doesn't necessarily reflect how well the veteran has been pitching for the Twins this season. Besides one abysmal start against the Royals in which he allowed seven runs, Pavano has been a bright spot in the rotation -- having not allowed more than two earned runs in six of his seven starts and pitching at least six innings in each of those outings. But it hasn't resulted in wins since Pavano has received the least run support of all the Twins starters. Having allowed just two runs over seven innings against the White Sox in his last start, Pavano will next face the Blue Jays. He is 3-4 with a 5.59 ERA in nine career starts against Toronto.

home_pitcher_note: One of the biggest surprises in the Major Leagues during the first month and half of the season, Fister hopes to continue his state-of-the-art pitching against the visiting Blue Jays as the Mariners begin a homestand. Fister ranks third in the American League in ERA and is a close second to Cliff Lee as the most consistent starter in the Seattle rotation. He was put to a stern test in his previous start, holding the Rays to one run over five tough innings. A high pitch count got him out of the game, not the Rays hitters. He has struck out 20 batters and walked nine in seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cecil gave up hits to his first four batters in his start against the Texas Rangers on Friday. Not surprisingly, he lasted two innings and was raked for eight hits and eight earned runs along with two walks. The eight earned runs were the most Cecil has allowed in his big league career and it was the shortest start of his career. But the Blue Jays had their aerial game working, and five home runs helped overcome Cecil's subpar outing to produce a 16-10 victory and present him with a no-decision. Fortunately for Cecil, he won't have to face the Rangers this time. He has allowed 15 earned runs over seven innings in two career starts against Texas.

home_pitcher_note: Saturday in Tampa Bay was same old, same old for Vargas, who allowed just two runs and four hits through seven innings but took a no-decision after a late bullpen mistake and lack of run support led to a 3-2 loss. In his seven outings, the Mariners have scored two runs four times, making life difficult during his string of six straight quality starts. Vargas and Doug Fister have been Seattle's pleasant surprises, and after showing consistency, it's time to stop regarding their success as lucky starts to the season.
away_pitcher_note: Romero saw his season ERA plummet from 3.42 to 2.88 over the course or nine crisp innings at home against the Rangers on Saturday afternoon. The left-hander completed the first shutout of his young career, holding Texas' potent lineup to five hits (all singles) with just one walk issued. Along the way, Romero matched a career high with 12 strikeouts. Romero featured a strong changeup, as well as an effective, curve, cutter and fastball. He concentrated on throwing to the middle of the plate, allowing his strong pitch movement to do the rest. It worked, considering Romero threw 70 percent (81-for-116) of his pitches for strikes. Romero threw one ball or fewer to 24 of the 32 hitters he faced. The strong performance came after the sophomore yielded 12 runs on 21 hits with 11 walks over 17 1/3 innings across his previous three turns. Romero has gone 1-0 with a 5.11 ERA in two career games against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Haren had a really rough outing against the Braves on Sunday and afterward said: "That's as bad as I've been as a Diamondback probably." He gave up seven runs (six earned) in a season-low 4 1/3 innings on eight hits and three walks. It was the fourth time in nine starts Haren had given up four-plus runs in an outing and the second time he's been charged with seven runs. In six career starts against the Blue Jays, he is 4-1 with a 5.77 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Thankfully Morrow bounced back against the Rangers on Sunday following his disastrous outing vs. Boston on May 10, when he was shelled for six runs over just 1 2/3 innings. The right-hander held a potent Rangers offense to just two runs over six innings, with eight strikeouts. What made the outing more encouraging is that Morrow only issued one walk, as oppose to the six he unleashed against the Red Sox. The key for Morrow, who has electric stuff, is to become more consistent with his new delivery -- a lowered arm slot -- and limit the walks which have plagued him from time to time this season. Morrow has only lost once this season when he issues two or fewer free passes, going 3-1 over that span.  Morrow will square off against the D-backs on Friday, a team he has yet to face over his four-year career.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson finally had his first dominant start in a D-backs uniform. The 26-year-old hurled eight shutout innings in a win against the Marlins on Monday night while striking out a career-high 12 batters. Jackson had a no-hitter through four, put only two runners in scoring position and retired six of the last seven batters he faced -- five via strikeout. What's perhaps most impressive is that Jackson didn't really have much command of his fastball, especially early on. His success was mainly the result of a slider that was cutting better than it has all season. For his career against the Blue Jays, Jackson is 2-3 with a 3.82 ERA in 12 games (11 starts).
away_pitcher_note: For the second straight game, Eveland was unable to pitch beyond the fourth inning, on his way to earning his third loss of the season. Eveland surrendered five runs -- three earned -- while giving up nine hits and four walks against the Twins on Monday. While Eveland was unspectacular to say the least, he was also the victim of some poor defense. First baseman Lyle Overbay made two crucial errors on a single play in the fourth inning, resulting in a four-run frame to chase Eveland from the ballgame. Eveland has now allowed eight walks, 15 hits and nine runs over his past two starts. In his career, Eveland is 0-1 with a 0.00 ERA over three relief appearances against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Making his first start of the season after some success in the Minor Leagues, Bucker gave up two runs in five innings but suffered the loss against the Marlins on Tuesday, when Josh Johnson hurled seven shutout innings. Buckner had trouble the second time through the order, and his control failed him in the fourth, when he allowed a run during a six-pitch stretch that saw him issue two hit-by-pitches and a walk. In the fifth, he surrendered back-to-back two-out doubles off the left-field wall. The 26-year-old gave up six hits and threw 56 of his 90 pitches for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: The Blue Jays have gotten exactly what they need from their ace. He has eight quality starts in nine tries, the Jays have won in his last four starts, and all three of his wins have come following losses. In addition, his tip helped straighten out Brandon Morrow's mechanics, and that's just the type of leadership Toronto wants from its big arm. He followed up a seven-inning, two-hit shutout in Boston by going another seven against Minnesota and allowing just one run, and hell hope to keep that momentum rolling against the D-backs, one of baseball's highest-scoring teams.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders has put together three exceptional starts in the wake of three bad ones, showing that he has regained command and trust in his stuff. He shut down the White Sox on four hits and one earned run on Wednesday night, striking out four while walking two men. He kept his fastball in good locations and kept the ball in the park, never an easy task at U.S. Cellular Field. In those past three starts he has yielded two earned runs across 22 1/3 innings. Saunders shut out the Blue Jays across eight innings in a win at Toronto on April 17 and is 2-3, 3.76 in six career starts against the Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Cecil rebounded from a rough start with a solid performance on the road against the Mariners on Wednesday. The lefty was charged with two runs on seven hits over 6 1/3 innings, during which he struck out four and walked two en route to a win. In his previous outing, Cecil allowed eight runs in just two innings at home against Texas. Remove that subpar showing against the Rangers and Cecil has fashioned a 2.75 ERA in the month of May. The southpaw has never faced the Angels.
summary: 2010-05-24 - Toronto Blue Jays (6) @ Los Angeles Angels (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Ryu faced Boston on April 20, giving up eight hits and four earned runs over five innings. The lefty owns a 0-2 record with a 4.24 ERA in three career starts against the Red Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez gave up four runs over six innings in a loss to the Athletics on Wednesday. In 15 career appearances against Toronto, the lefty is 5-4 with a 4.52 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: After a slow start, Richards has been on fire of late. In his last four starts, the righty is 3-0 with a 2.16 ERA. He is 2-5 with a 5.49 ERA in nine career games (seven starts) against Toronto.
summary: 2021-05-19 - Boston Red Sox (7) @ Toronto Blue Jays (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Matz tossed his first scoreless start of the season last time out in a no-decision against the Phillies on Friday. It was a continuance of his up-and-down season, as he allowed just three runs in his first three outings, then 17 runs over his next four.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta has been Boston's best starting pitcher so far this season. Opponents are hitting .189 against him. Pivetta has allowed two earned runs or fewer in six of his eight starts.
summary: 2021-05-20 - Boston Red Sox (8) @ Toronto Blue Jays (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kay is fighting to keep a rotation spot for another turn through, and made a fine case last time out with four shutout innings. His next step is finding his strikeout pitch earlier to be more efficient and work deeper against the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Glasnow is coming off another gem: an eight-inning, 10-strikeout performance against the Mets last Friday. He's pitched like an ace, but his worst start came against Toronto at The Trop on April 23: six innings, five runs, two homers, 10 strikeouts.
summary: 2021-05-21 - Tampa Bay Rays (9) @ Toronto Blue Jays (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Ray threw 112 pitches in his last outing as he battled through 5 2/3 innings. He's struck out nine or more batters in four of his last five outings this season and has drastically cut down his walks in 2021, which was a major issue for him in '20.
away_pitcher_note: McClanahan gave up four runs on two homers, both hit off hanging sliders, in 5 1/3 innings Saturday vs. the Mets. The rookie lefty has struck out 22 of the 72 batters he's faced while only walking five. This will be his first time facing Toronto.
summary: 2021-05-22 - Tampa Bay Rays (3) @ Toronto Blue Jays (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Ryu is pitching as well as he has since joining the Blue Jays, and is coming off seven shutout innings against Boston. The ace lives near 90 mph, but even his own coaches have a hard time guessing which pitch he'll throw next lately.
away_pitcher_note: After dealing with right hamstring tightness, Wacha will be reinstated from the 10-day IL to start. He hasn't faced the Blue Jays since 2017, when he allowed two runs over six innings in a winning effort.
summary: 2021-05-23 - Tampa Bay Rays (6) @ Toronto Blue Jays (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Thornton has made 14 appearances and has done well, limiting batters to 21 hits and eight walks in 23.1 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Yarbrough allowed six runs (three earned) in six innings Wednesday in Baltimore. He has been excellent when pitching multiple innings after an opener (2-0, 1.00 ERA in four outings) but has struggled as a traditional starter (0-3, 6.28 ERA in five starts).
summary: 2021-05-24 - Tampa Bay Rays (14) @ Toronto Blue Jays (8) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: Matz is coming off a rough outing against the Red Sox and is still looking to stabilize things after a hot April and cold May. He pounded the zone last time out, but will need to find a way to miss bats and create weaker contact.

summary: 2021-05-27 - Toronto Blue Jays (2) @ New York Yankees (0) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: After pitching into the seventh inning just twice in his first six starts, Ryu has now done so in each of his past three, posting a 1.31 ERA in that span. His last road start came May 12 at Atlanta, where he allowed one run in seven innings.
summary: 2021-05-28 - Toronto Blue Jays @ Cleveland Indians (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Fresh off eight-plus innings and what was then an AL-best seventh win, Civale is giving the team what it desperately needs right now: dependability and consistency.

home_pitcher_note: Hentges had to wait an extra day to get his start after expected inclement weather postponed Saturday's game. The righty is hoping to carry the momentum he established last time out, going a career-high five innings with seven strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: After notching a season-high 10 strikeouts in his last start -- a road win over the Yankees -- Matz will face Cleveland for only the third time in his career. In the previous two outings, he is 2-0 with a 0.68 ERA and 16 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Ray wasn't as sharp last time out, and the home run ball continues to be a problem, with 10 allowed over 29 1/3 innings in May. He's still pounding the zone, though, as he reinvents his pitching style in 2021.
away_pitcher_note: Alcantara is coming off his longest outing of the year -- an eight-inning effort against the Phillies in which he allowed just two runs on two hits but took the loss. He's allowed two earned runs or fewer in eight of 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: What can Manoah do for an encore? The club's No. 5 prospect dominated the Yankees with six shutout innings in his debut, and when his fastball-slider mix is combined with his aggression on the mound, Manoah puts on a show.
away_pitcher_note: It’s not reflected in his 1-3 record this season, but López has allowed just four runs on 15 hits with three walks and 16 strikeouts in 19 innings over his past three starts. This will be his first career start against the Blue Jays.

home_pitcher_note: Ryu's last outing was him at his best, even if it didn't show in the stat line, as he battled ugly weather in Cleveland to earn the win. With a 2.62 ERA and some of the best control he's ever shown, the ace is absolutely locked in.
away_pitcher_note: After going four innings in three consecutive starts, Greinke is 2-1 with a 2.45 ERA and 0.77 WHIP in his last three starts, two of which were eight innings. He struck out 17 batters and walked only four in his last 22 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Stripling carried a 7.20 ERA into late May, but has allowed just one run over 12 innings in his last two starts. Serious adjustments have been made, so now it's a matter of sustaining this newfound success.
away_pitcher_note: Urquidy returned from an 18-day stint on the injured list and held the Red Sox to one run and three hits in six innings Monday. He's 4-0 with a 1.53 ERA and 0.71 WHIP in his last five starts, during which the Astros are 5-0.

home_pitcher_note: Matz's up-and-down season has settled in at a 4.22 ERA, but the lefty is never far from a standout performance. Keep an eye on his velocity, which ticked up as he struck out 10 back on May 25.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia is 4-0 with a 1.57 ERA in his last four starts, throwing a career-high seven innings of one-run ball against the Red Sox in his last start. His 2.60 ERA through his first 10 career starts is seventh-lowest in Astros history.

home_pitcher_note: Rodón wasn’t as sharp as he has been all season during his last start, allowing five runs (including three homers) over six innings against the Indians. But Rodón still struck out eight and walked one, giving his team a chance.
away_pitcher_note: Ray's changes in '21 have become the new normal for him -- walking very few while racking up the strikeouts. He's also providing length with at least six innings pitched in six of his last eight outings.
summary: 2021-06-08 - Toronto Blue Jays (1) @ Chicago White Sox (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lynn is 1-3 with a 5.45 ERA in seven career games (six starts) against Toronto. But the right-hander is 6-0 with a 1.38 ERA and a .150 opponents average over his past seven starts. Lynn has 36 strikeouts in his last 39 innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: Manoah was dominant in his debut then struggled in his encore, so this is his shot to find a groove. The No. 5 prospect is brimming with confidence and will benefit from spotting his fastball better in Chicago after allowing some hard contact in his last start.
summary: 2021-06-09 - Toronto Blue Jays (6) @ Chicago White Sox (2) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: Ryu's last outing was very uncharacteristic, allowing six earned runs over 5 2/3 innings. He felt he was rushing his delivery, so look for the ace to bounce back after having some time to evaluate that.
summary: 2021-06-10 - Toronto Blue Jays (2) @ Chicago White Sox (5) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: Over Stripling's first six starts, he posted a 7.20 ERA. In the three outings since, it's been 1.06. Stripling looks like a different pitcher, which he'll need to be to keep rolling at Fenway Park.
summary: 2021-06-11 - Toronto Blue Jays (5) @ Boston Red Sox (6) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: Matz has run hot and cold this season but feels like he's very close to more consistency. His stuff is certainly there, so Matz shouldn't need a major adjustment to make it all click.
summary: 2021-06-12 - Toronto Blue Jays (7) @ Boston Red Sox (2) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: The reinvented Ray struck out 13 in his last outing. After an incredible turnaround in his control, Ray is turning the clock back to that excellent 2017 season.
summary: 2021-06-13 - Toronto Blue Jays (18) @ Boston Red Sox (4) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: Manoah bounced back in his third MLB outing against the White Sox and gets another tough American League East test after dominating the Yankees in his debut back on May 27.
summary: 2021-06-14 - Toronto Blue Jays (1) @ Boston Red Sox (2) (Final)

summary: 2021-06-17 - New York Yankees (8) @ Toronto Blue Jays (4) (Final)
